in_arabic.name: إمانة
in_arabic.long_meaning: الإيمانة هي مصدر الإيمان، ويرجع هذا الاسم إلى الجذور الألف-الميم-النون، ويُستخدم للإشارة إلى الشخص المؤمن والمؤمنة بالله ورسوله، ويُعتبر هذا الاسم شرفياً في الإسلام، ويُستخدم في اللغة العربية للإشارة إلى الصدق والعدل والمعرفة، وله علاقة قريبة بالconceptualization الإسلامية للدين والواقع، ويرمز إلى الصبر والثبات في الإيمان، ويتعارف في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأعراف، ويعتبر من أسماء الله الحسنى، وينسب للبعض من أهل الصفة

in_urdu.name: امानत

in_english.name: Emaanat
in_english.meaning: Faithfulness to God and His messenger, sincerity, and trustworthiness
in_english.long_meaning: Emaanat is a name that represents faithfulness to God and His messenger, sincerity, and trustworthiness. It is derived from the Arabic root 'A-L-M', which means faith, trust, and loyalty. In Islamic tradition, emaanat is considered a virtue and a quality of a true believer. It is mentioned in the Quran as a characteristic of those who are righteous and close to God. Emaanat is also associated with the concept of tawhid, or the oneness of God. In modern times, emaanat is used as a name for boys and girls, and is considered a symbol of faith and devotion to God.

The name embodies the importance of unwavering religious faith and trust in Allah, and the Day of Judgment. Naming a child Emaanat in Islamic culture is a testament to the parents' deep faith and belief in God's sovereignty, guidance, and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Emaanat is a reminder of the essential foundation of Islamic belief: faith and trust in Allah. It signifies the importance of placing faith and trust in Allah alone, and not relying on worldly matters for security or happiness. The name also represents the inner strength and patience required to maintain faith and belief in the face of challenges and trials. In essence, the name Emaanat echoes the Islamic belief in the concept of Tawakkul (trust and reliance on Allah), and is an inspiration for the bearer to strive towards living a life that embodies this spiritual principle.
